transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The White House has issued a warning to Democrats over their plans to investigate the Trump
administration.
White House counsel Will Scharf issued the warning in a letter to California Democratic
Congressman Robert Garcia, who will likely chair the powerful House Oversight Committee
in the new Congress.
Scharf said such investigations may amount to "blatant criminality."
Garcia said Congress's investigative powers do not need the permission of the White House.
Texas Democrats say they're open to working with Elon Musk.
Michael Adkisson with Houston Public Media says the founder of Tesla and SpaceX poured
millions of dollars into Republican races in the state.
Musk had grown close to Texas Republicans, like Governor Greg Abbott, who advocated for
tax breaks and public investments.
He spent more than $200 million on them this election cycle.
Now, Texas Democrats say they're open to working with Musk, with some stipulations.
Here's Governor-elect Gina Inajosa speaking on CNN.
We can have a strong working relationship with Elon Musk and his companies, but it has
to be on our terms.
It cannot be just running over the people of Texas.
And that's what changes now that I will be governor.
Musk said on social media that SpaceX and Tesla prospered in Texas, "because we were
not constantly operating under an oppressive and extractive state government."
For NPR News, I'm Michael Adkisson in Houston.
Peace talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have ended without a breakthrough.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports President Trump's envoys now travel from Abu Dhabi to
Moscow to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"Head U.S. negotiator and President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner told the media they
had seen some openings and opportunities, but few in Ukraine believe a window for serious
diplomacy has opened.
Skeptical Ukrainian negotiators were instructed to approach the talks with an open mind if
only to avoid annoying President Trump.
Ukrainians do not believe the Kremlin will miss the opportunity to pummel Ukraine's severely
weakened energy infrastructure in this fifth winter of the war.
Analysts say Trump is looking for a foreign policy win after his midterm drubbing, but
Putin has not backed off any of his maximalist demands, such as Kiev handing over territory
Russia has been unable to conquer."
Eleanor Beardsley in PR News, Kiev.
Treasury Secretary Scott Besant is calling for more balance between the U.S. and China,
and PR's Scott Horsley reports.
Treasury Secretary Scott Besant says the U.S. needs to produce more, and China needs to
consume more.
Besant spoke at a New York gala last night ahead of President Trump's visit to Shenzhen
next week, where he'll meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
China's consumption is likely to get a boost from Singles Day, which starts today.
The online shopping promotion is a kind of cross between Prime Day, Black Friday and
Valentine's Day.
Scott Horsley in PR News, Washington.
A rebound for A.I. stocks lifted the U.S. market today.
The S&P 500 rose more than one-quarter percent.
It's NPR News.
Former President Joe Biden says he didn't know he had cancer while he was president and wouldn't
have sought a second term if he'd already been diagnosed.
The comments came in an interview with People magazine before the release of his memoir.
Biden was diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer months after leaving office in 2025.
His campaign ended after a disastrous debate performance against then-candidate Donald Trump.
Hundreds of schools in Italy, Scotland, Ireland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats.
NPR's Ruth Sherlock reports on what appears to be the latest coordinated effort to sow
chaos and disruption across Europe.
Police in Northern Ireland said the more than 300 affected schools received the same chilling
email.
A copy of the message sent to Italian schools seen by NPR said, "I have prepared for this
for a long time, to kill every one of you."
It said an explosive with a remote detonator had been placed in the building.
The message caused panic in schools with many evacuating.
Police in Scotland and Northern Ireland described the message as a hoax.
Italy's Defense Minister Guido Crocito said it was part of an effort to create panic and
disruption in European countries.
For NPR News, I'm Ruth Sherlock in London.
An ocean liner that was once the fastest on the seas is headed to its final home on the
floor of the Gulf of Mexico as the world's largest artificial reef.
Officials have begun the process of sinking the SS United States today, about 25 miles
southwest of Destin, Florida between Panama City and Pensacola, the 990 foot ship set
a speed record in 1952.
This is NPR.
